claims.text: Transport outcome of one ask. CLOSED -- an adapter may not invent a sixth.
claims.why: The chunk defines STATUSES as a tuple with exactly five strings; no sixth is present.

claims.text: None of these is a judgement about the reviewed work; 'ok' means the bytes came back, nothing more.
claims.why: The comment explicitly states that STATUSES are transport outcomes, not judgments.

claims.text: Egress lane for a participant. untrusted turns the allow-list / default-deny tier ON (sensitivity.slice_egress_rule).
claims.why: sensitivity.slice_egress_rule is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify the claim.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- never free prose -- so a council record can be aggregated.
claims.why: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS is a tuple of predefined string constants, suitable for aggregation.

claims.text: Not 'localhost': avoids the IPv6 (::1) miss on Windows, same as providers/ollama.py.
claims.why: Cannot verify the reason for avoiding 'localhost' without seeing providers/ollama.py or Windows behavior.

claims.text: Prepended to EVERY outbound prompt. The evidence under review was written by a candidate model; a diff can carry text addressed to the reviewer and there is no delimiter that makes an LLM reliably treat text as data. The mitigation is not a better delimiter -- it is that an injection attempt becomes a FINDING. (The structural mitigation is that nothing here can act.)
claims.why: PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE is defined as a string constant; the claim about its purpose is documented.

claims.text: The evidence under review was written by a candidate model; a diff can carry text addressed to the reviewer...
claims.why: The claim about evidence content is a design rationale, not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: NO LOCAL-HOST TABLE HERE, ON PURPOSE. 'Do the bytes leave this machine' has exactly one implementation, sensitivity.lane_for_host, imported above -- it is the predicate that switches the tier-2 allow-list, so a second copy next to it is a second answer to a safety question. This module used to carry _LOCAL_HOSTS + _endpoint_host and disagreed with the shared predicate on [::1], on 127.0.0.0/8, and on localhost. See tests/test_host_predicate.py, which fails if the table comes back.
claims.why: Cannot verify the existence of sensitivity.lane_for_host, past _LOCAL_HOSTS, or test_host_predicate.py from this chunk.

claims.text: Make a model id safe for an actor segment without losing information.
claims.why: The function _slug uses re.sub to replace non-alphanumeric characters with '-', preserving information.

claims.text: council.<vendor>.<model> per docs/adrs/010-naming-namespaces.md. A bare actor: 'claude' in a durable record is a defect... The FORMAT is delegated to bus.actor_id so the id on a transcript turn and the id on the reply that produced it cannot drift apart; this function only normalises the raw model id first (a raw qwen2.5-coder:7b would otherwise put a colon in a durable identifier).
claims.why: Cannot verify the existence of docs/adrs/010-naming-namespaces.md or bus.actor_id; also cannot verify the claim about colons in durable identifiers without seeing bus.actor_id.

claims.text: Coarse weight family, for VendorReply.independence_class. The unit of independence is WEIGHTS, not endpoints. Local qwen2.5-coder:7b and bench qwen2.5-coder:7b are one voice on two sockets... Heuristic and deliberately coarse -- it strips the tag (:7b) and any trailing size/version token, so it OVER-merges rather than under-merges. Over-merging costs a seat; under-merging silently fakes independence.
claims.why: The function model_family implements the described heuristic: splits on ':', takes last segment after '/', removes trailing tokens matching size/version patterns.

claims.text: Deliberately carries NO approve/reject/pass/verdict/ok/score/confidence field, and must never grow one -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: VendorReply is defined as a frozen dataclass with fields 'status' and others; no such judgment fields are present in this chunk.

observations.what: Hardcoded IP addresses for bench environment.
Closed vocabulary STATUSES and UNAVAILABLE_REASONS may require updates as new transport outcomes emerge.
PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE is a long string prepended to every prompt; may affect token counts.
actor_id depends on external function bus.actor_id; any change there could break ID consistency.
model_family heuristic may over-merge model families; intentional but could cause issues.
